extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (schools, colleges, universities), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX training and recordkeeping compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for who must be trained on Title IX obligations, what topics trainings must cover, how trainings may be delivered, special rules for students with disabilities, and recordkeeping and retention obligations under §§106.8(d)–(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training required for all employees (§106.8(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.8(d)(1) requires all employees to be trained on a recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination in its education program or activity, the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination, and all applicable notification and information requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is affirmative (train all employees), not merely make training available. The Department recognizes some burden but considers training all employees important to ensure understanding of roles and responsibilities when they obtain information about conduct that may reasonably constitute sex discrimination. The Department assumes training will often be incorporated into existing annual trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of non-employee personnel directly involved in Title IX duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department notes that §106.8(d)(1) includes any advisors, graduate students, contractors, volunteers, or third-party agents who are performing roles that are directly involved in carrying out the recipient's Title IX duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate training for non-employees not directly involved in carrying out Title IX duties because costs would not be justified, but recognizes that local employment arrangements may render some of these persons employees who must be trained. Recipients may choose to train volunteers, contractors, or other non-employees where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training must be provided, not merely made available
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(d) requires a recipient to train all employees, as opposed to just making training available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even where collective bargaining agreements exist; the Department disagrees that such agreements preclude offering and enforcing training, citing the 2020 amendments' similar requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on the definition of 'sex-based harassment' (§106.8(d)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: All employee training must include the definition of 'sex-based harassment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This training applies only to employees (not students) and is considered essential to a recipient's ability to identify and address conduct that constitutes sex discrimination. Objections about statutory authority were rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on notification requirements for pregnancy or related conditions (§106.8(d)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must be trained regarding their obligations under §106.40(b)(2) to students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The training is modest and for most employees will focus on: (1) promptly notifying a student (or person with legal authority to act on the student's behalf) that the Title IX Coordinator can take actions to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access; and (2) sharing the Title IX Coordinator's contact information. Training for all employees is required because students may disclose to any employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility of training delivery (live/virtual/asynchronous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training need not be conducted in-person and may be provided online or virtually, synchronously or asynchronously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate a particular method of providing training; regardless of delivery method, the training must satisfy the requirements of §106.8(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for individuals authorized to modify or terminate supportive measures (§106.8(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have the authority to modify or terminate supportive measures under §106.44(g)(4) must receive training on specified additional topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision targets a narrow category of employees (e.g., deans or principals) who can modify or reverse decisions about supportive measures; because of their decisionmaking authority they must receive tailored training on the additional topics set forth in §106.8(d)(2). The Department declined requests to remove or broaden this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient must require consultation with IEP/Section 504 team members for K–12 students with disabilities (§106.8(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For elementary or secondary students with disabilities who are a complainant or respondent, the recipient must require that the Title IX Coordinator consult with one or more members, as appropriate, of the student's IEP team or Section 504 team 'to determine how to comply' with relevant special education laws while carrying out Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(e) does not require IEP or Section 504 meetings, full-team consultation, identification of which team members must participate, or specific timing; those choices are left to recipient discretion. The consultation must be sensitive and consistent with FERPA. The Title IX Coordinator's duties are delegable, so a designee may engage in consultation. The recipient is responsible for ensuring consultation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary students with disabilities — consultation optional
rubrics_metrics.description: For postsecondary students, §106.8(e) permits, but does not require, consultation between the Title IX Coordinator and the institution's office designated to provide supports to students with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to require postsecondary institutions to provide advisors or to mandate consultation with disability services offices, preserving flexibility and student autonomy. Recipients may nevertheless consult or provide additional supports where appropriate and must still comply with other federal disability laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX limited to sex discrimination — other disability accommodation obligations remain
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX and its implementing regulations are limited to addressing sex discrimination and do not impose obligations or requirements that are conferred by the IDEA, ADA, or Section 504.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must continue to comply with the IDEA, Section 504, Title II and III of the ADA, and their implementing regulations regarding reasonable modifications, auxiliary aids and services, and effective communication. The Department will continue to enforce those statutes separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping—maintenance of documentation (§106.8(f)(1) and (2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must maintain records regarding complaints of sex discrimination, the actions the recipient took to meet its obligations in response to notification to the Title IX Coordinator of conduct that reasonably may be sex discrimination, and materials used to provide training under §106.8(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping helps reveal compliance practices and patterns of noncompliance. Records should document informal resolution processes, grievance procedures, dismissals, and resulting outcomes. The provision is limited to maintaining records and making training materials available for public inspection upon request; FERPA and §106.44(j) govern disclosure of personally identifiable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period — seven years
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department maintains that seven years is an appropriate period for maintaining records required under §106.8(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may retain records for a longer period if they choose or if other legal obligations require it. The Department declined to tie retention to student enrollment length or litigation needs because a standard fixed threshold is administrable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of recordkeeping tied to notification to the Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The recordkeeping requirement in §106.8(f)(2) is tied to notification of information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination — i.e., records of which the Title IX Coordinator has notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to expand §106.8(f)(2) to apply whenever a recipient has actual or constructive notice. Under §106.44(c), employees are required either to notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have such information or to provide the reporter with the Title IX Coordinator's contact information, so notification will occur through those mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on compelled sharing, deletion, correction, and demographic collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to share evidentiary records to assist in lawsuits or OCR investigations, to delete or correct records when complaints are dismissed or informal resolution concludes without a finding, or to collect demographic data of complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department lacks authority to fine recipients for failure to maintain or share records and notes that evidentiary sharing obligations to OCR are already governed by 34 CFR 100.6(c) (incorporated by §106.81). The Department also declined to solicit demographic data collection without a specific proposal and public comment.
